A hidden gem across from disappointment!. I went to Dongdaemun specifically for the smoked duck place across the street that gets all the attention. *That was a complete disaster! 

Then I crossed the street and walked upstairs to Dongbuk Hwa Gwa Wang, and discovered the real reason to come to this block!

This is genuine Northern Chinese cuisine the kind you rarely see in Seoul. The menu is 13 pages, fully illustrated, with explanations in both Chinese and English. The staff couldn’t have been kinder. When I sat down they brought me a huge 13 page menu that described each dish (with pictures) after studying the menu for 10 minutes, I realized the “special duck” wasn’t on this menu and I was in the wrong place !! 😳 Wow, 🫢they laughed it off and kindly showed me where the place was that I had intended to have lunch, wishing me well with smiles on their faces, they couldn’t have been sweeter . 
Off I went to get that “special” DUCK and that is a whole other story ….😵‍💫 but suffice to say don’t want to go there. You will thank me for warning you (btw I have posted a review of regarding that meal) 

So long story short after I left the duck place (a HUGE mistake going there), I came back to this restaurant, intending to maybe take a couple bites of a one of the dishes that intrigued me and then bring it home as “carry out” because I just finished eating at that duck place, their not so special duck and my taste buds were killed and my appetite was kind of shot anyways they welcomed me back like a regular.
I ordered the sizzling iron-plate beef. They brought it out covered in tinfoil and warned me not to open it until the sizzling stopped, or I’d burn myself. When I finally lifted the foil, the plate was heaped about five inches high tender beef stir-fried with bok choy, beautiful whole mushrooms, vibrant red peppers, onions, and scallions, all caught in a glossy savory sauce. The plate literally couldn’t hold any more food. Crispy, hot, deeply flavorful every bite earned.
The contrast with the smoked duck place across the street was night and day. 17,000원 here for a meal I couldn’t finish, versus 40,000원 across the street for a meal I regretted. Better food, better value, better people. Top-notch customer service from start to finish.
If you’re in Dongdaemun and looking for something that isn’t the usual Korean BBQ or hotteok crawl, skip the duck place. Go upstairs across the street instead. You’ll eat better, pay less, and be treated like family. I’m coming back the next chance I get there are at least seven other things on that menu I still want to try.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ I’m sorry I didn’t take a picture of it when it first came to the table, I had intended to, but I was just so amazed that I dug right in and didn’t stop until I realized I had overate, it was that good!

It constantly amazes me how high end Parisian restaurants intentionally mistreat their guests.. I have lived half of my life in Paris and it constantly amazes me how high end restaurants intentionally mistreat their guests. 

First of all our Entree and Main Course were wonderful and if that were the criteria for my review it would be Five Star, but the entire staff were more like gatekeepers at a prison than waiters and hosts. 

I speak fluent French and yet everyone insisted on speaking to me in broken English. 

We were taken up several narrow stairways to a room where they confine the tourist and granted there were some that deserved to be there. 

The better dining rooms downstairs are off limits to us. We were seated in a room with only cursory comfort. There was a very loud speaker behind our table playing annoying disco music so the candlelight was diminished significantly. 

The waiter and hostess showed their teeth but never smiled. There was an ever present air of destain in their every action. 

I asked the waiter if this room was set aside for tourists and he was visible shaken but an idiotic grin remained constant as he denied that that was the case. 

There was a very brief moment when the canned Music was turned off and an Asian woman sat at a piano and sang about six soft versions of American and French songs …but we soon realized why she was there. Four times during her set she abruptly changed the melody to “Happy Birthday to you” and suddenly we were all transported to children’s party restaurant as all of the cell phones came out and people clapped and sang. 

Her duty done she left …and the canned disco music was put back on. 

One waiter knocked over a bottle of water on our table and soaked the entire surface. He refused to change the cloth and repeatedly placed napkins over the spill soaking each until after the fifth it was only wet. 

The hostesses at the entrances of these grand salons are more monsters at the gate than hostesses. They also show their teeth without smiling and condescend to herd the patrons to the various rooms that they and only they deem appropriate. 

The Soufflé on the menu is not a soufflé it was what is called “Lava Cake” elsewhere, a mass of reheated raw batter of chocolate in a copper terrine with a shiny crust. 

The bill came to nearly $500 and still we were asked to add a tip. Most people don’t realize that the service and taxes are included in France ..,so when they are presented the the portable payment portal they are asked to add 15% 20% or ever 25% and they usually crack under the pressure of the moment and they never see a small button at the bottom that says “no thank you” which I chose. 

I have lived in and visited Paris often over the past 50 years and now I’m 71 years old and I think I am finally weary of doing battle. 

M Dane

Unfortunately, on Saturday, February 21, 2026 around 2 PM a friend and I had planned a girls day out luncheon. We wanted seafood so we decided to go to Wintzell's. I indicated to her that I had promised the management at the restaurant in Greenville last month that I would give the one in MGM another chance, since we had been advised they were under new corporate management. Regretfully, their quality and service has not improved. The restaurant was severely understaffed, as it had been since the pandemic when their service, quality, and health dept scores began to decline. After waiting at the hostess station to be seated for several minutes we decided to sit at the crowded bar. The guy tending the bar (Cornelius) was being required to attend customers at the bar and seated in the restaurant at tables. He was friendly, polite, customer focused and oriented as he attempted to handle such unreasonable demand. We really felt sorry for him. reviews.text:
Excellent service, beautiful resort. We stayed at the resort for one week towards the end of January
I can honestly say what made our stay the best was because of our amazing butlers Linda and Freddy.
Each morning they sent us a good morning message as well as an itinerary for the day for the hotel showing what activities were planned and where, and what restaurants were open for what hours.
In the afternoon they also sent us a reminder text for any reservations we may have for dinner.
Upon arrival they promptly greeted us and assisted us with making all reservations for the week.
They were very kind and considerate and always asking us if there was anything we needed or they could help with and if we did have any request they responded promptly.
During our time I also had services performed at the spa.
The hydrotherapy session was nice however I do have to say the pools were a little bit colder than we had anticipated therefore we were not able to use those.
We did however enjoy sitting on the rooftop deck enjoying juice shots and smoothies from the healthy bar
The massage service I received was amazing I had a massage facial and sugar scrub it was very nice.
We did have a swim up room which we really were not able to use much because the water was colder than we had anticipated, we understand this is their winter and the pools are not well heated however we just were not anticipating the water to be as cold as it was.
Our room however was very clean and well stocked, each day they came to refresh whatever items we had eaten out of the mini bar and they asked us what our preferences were to ensure each day they restocked with our favorites.
Overall I would definitely recommend

reviews.text:
Amazing deal for top notch, well-located hotel. I used to come to the diner here just for matzoh ball soup and pastrami sandwiches between shows. The hotel itself was considered a dive.
Well, it is under new ownership/management and they have transformed it into a gem.

The theme is art deco and there are murals depicting people of the era.

I stayed in a 9 floor room which overlooked 47th St but I didn’t hear any traffic noise. The room itself was in great shape, with what looked like new furniture. Two complementary water bottles and a coffee maker are provided and replenished every day. The bathroom was very clean, well-equipped and orderly with a walk-in shower. The water pressure was fine. The blow dryers are highll quality. There was even a robe in the closet. A large umbrella is also in the closet to borrow.

I was fascinated by the lighting. All of the lightbulbs are Edison bulbs. Lamps turn on and off with touch, which really impressed me.
Besides a regular shade, there is a blackout shade you can pull down, which is great to keep the city lights out at night.

The gym is more than adequate, with new machines and anything else you need.

On top of everything, this one of the most inexpensive hotels I’ve ever stayed in in Manhattan. I wholeheartedly recommend it.

My husband politely stood up and simply smiled at the manger/owner and then he realized that we had been sitting at the bar area for a long time. So he reminded the host that we had been waiting longer. Thank God we didn’t have to wait longer. This is a small restaurant so the seating is tight and their prices are a bit high, but we enjoyed our perfect Christmas Eve dinner so much!! We have already been referring our friends to visit Broil if they’re ever in the lower Keys! This restaurant is really a “hidden gem”. It’s worth every penny!!
